span.p:
Confirmed
+ WHICH challenge was used
(4 named + 'other' free text, D57)

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Third party acting for them
MUST be named + relationship

color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(74, 47, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
L1_PROBABLE - caller ID matched
the whole record is ON SCREEN (D74),
but nothing may be said or acted on yet

div.style: color: rgb(51, 51, 51) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
brief shows action 0:
ยืนยันตัวตนผู้ติดต่อก่อนให้ข้อมูลกรมธรรม์

div.style: color: rgb(11, 37, 69) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
agent asks an OPEN question
ขอทราบชื่อผู้ติดต่อด้วยค่ะ

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
never ask a leading question (D55).
'ใช่คุณ X ไหมคะ' both leaks that the number
belongs to them AND is weaker verification -
anyone can answer yes. The name is on the
agent's screen; it does not leave their mouth.

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
agent presses one of THREE
which three are OFFERED depends on how
the caller was identified (D71)

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
L3_VERIFIED
outcome = confirmed
brief re-renders as v2

div.style: color: rgb(92, 26, 19) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
L0 + rejected id recorded
nothing re-proposes them
data-quality signal: usually
a recycled mobile number

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
L3_VERIFIED — it promotes (D65)
outcome stays third_party, forever

div.style: color: rgb(92, 26, 19) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
D65 REVERSED D42/D62 here. The button asserts the
agent checked this person may act for the policyholder,
so the LEVEL follows the attestation — same rule as
Confirmed. What keeps the log honest is the OUTCOME,
not a lower number: the record says 'an authorised
representative was verified', never 'the policyholder
was verified'. The earlier reading confused 'keep the log
truthful' with 'keep the level low', and only the first
was ever the requirement.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
a rejection is REVERSIBLE (D71). The original
resolution is kept, so an agent who pressed it by
mistake can put the caller back. Q18: with no customer
search yet, a rejected call otherwise stays anonymous
for its whole duration — the two forward outcomes are
DISABLED with the reason in the tooltip, not hidden.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 37, 69) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
the control LOCKS after every attestation (D61)
and is always reopenable with an explicit Amend.

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
the client knows a new one landed from
attestation_count, which only ever grows.
Watching attested_outcome misses a
confirmed → confirmed correction, and a lock
that opens once is worse than no lock —
the screen says the question is settled.

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
attestation log — append-only
what was asked, which challenge, who,
when, and the outcome. A THIRD-PARTY row
keeps the name and the relationship.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
a restart rebuilds attestation_count from this (D78).
A restore that came back empty would silently UNLOCK
an identity already attested — and a lock that opens
by itself is the worst of the three states.
